group_scores.rationale: NBS T1 releases (16-17 Nov, verified) show October retail sales +0.4% y/y, Jan-Oct FAI -8.1%, property investment -21.6%, private investment -11.4%; SCMP (20 Nov, verified via listing) reports the data missed expectations. NBS/gov.cn offer only existing-policy language and the PBoC held LPR at 3.0%/3.5% on 20 Nov (verified), so no policy backstop in window. BIS remote-access IFR (verified, effective 19 Nov) is a further mild negative for China internet/AI. Confidence capped at low: pillar unsaturated.
group_scores.falsifier: A State Council/MOF/NDRC stimulus package (2027 trade-in funding, special bonds, property destocking), an RRR or policy-rate cut before year-end, or an early-priced CEWC pledge.

group_scores.rationale: China weakness and the LPR hold are a modest drag via index weight only. The lead's premise of Korea/Taiwan-led EEM strength is contradicted by CNBC (Asia AI sell-off, Nasdaq -10% in the week), so the EEM vs MCHI gap remains unexplained. No score from price moves alone.
group_scores.falsifier: A verified non-China EM driver (Korea/Taiwan semis, India flows), a China stimulus surprise, or China weakness spilling into commodities and Asian supply chains.

group_scores.rationale: China industrial output (+4.8%) held up, limiting the hit to regional exporters. The BIS IFR (verified) adds license requirements for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand: a watch item for Southeast Asian data-center capex, but single primary source and no T2 market read.
group_scores.falsifier: T2 reports of license backlogs halting Southeast Asian data-center shipments (-1), or a verified Korea/Taiwan-led catalyst either way.
